name: rewind-selector-populated
opens_with: A four-turn seeded transcript, then double-Esc to open the selector on the newest turn
notes: iter-1659: the three existing rewind scenarios (rewind-selector, rewind-selector-filter, double-escape-over-a-draft) ALL render the empty state — none carries an agent_script, so no turn is ever seeded and the mark list stays empty in the sim. That means the corpus pinned only the 'No rewindable turns yet' render and NEVER the populated path iter-1633 changed: the pick-zone reversal over the whole turn block, the drop-zone dimming, the N-turn drop count, or the selected-row REVERSED modifier. The seeded script supplies four prompts (first/second/third/fourth) plus wrapped answers so the pick/drop zones span multiple rows and a zone boundary regression is visible as drift, not only as a unit-test assertion. MUTATION-PROVEN (2026-11-02): reverting iter-1633's pick zone to the prompt-row-only shape makes this style baseline DRIFT at exactly the selected row — expected `rgb:C58550/rgb:232832/r@4`, got `-@4`. The REVERSED modifier is the whole proof and it lives ONLY in the style layer, so a text-only baseline could not catch it. NOTE the deliberate asymmetry: this scenario does NOT drift when the DROP-zone mutation is applied, because the newest turn has nothing below it to drop (`sel_end` is `None`), so there is no dimmed region to break — correct discrimination, not a coverage gap; -navigate and -filter carry that half. The step() relation is NOT proven by these goldens (see the -filter notes). Pairs with rewind-selector-populated-navigate and rewind-selector-populated-filter.
